objects.description: Object identifier type used by PostgreSQL to identify many cataloged objects. Unsigned integer whose size matches unsigned int on the platform.
Deprecated alias formerly used in client APIs for a 64-bit signed integer. Prefer using int64_t directly.
Enumeration of libpq event kinds delivered to event procs registered with a PGconn.
Event payload for PGEVT_REGISTER; provides the PGconn being registered.
Event payload for PGEVT_CONNRESET; provides the PGconn that was reset.
Event payload for PGEVT_CONNDESTROY; provides the PGconn about to be destroyed.
Event payload for PGEVT_RESULTCREATE; includes the connection and the created PGresult.
Event payload for PGEVT_RESULTCOPY; includes source and destination PGresult objects.
Event payload for PGEVT_RESULTDESTROY; includes the PGresult being destroyed.
Callback type for libpq event handlers. Receives event id, event-specific payload, and passthrough pointer.

objects.description: Enumeration of connection states for PGconn objects.
Polling status codes used by nonblocking connection and cancel operations.

objects.description: Execution status of a PGresult produced by libpq.
Transaction status of a PGconn according to server state.
Controls verbosity of error messages returned by libpq.
Controls whether CONTEXT fields are included in error messages.
Status codes returned by PQping/PQpingParams indicating server reachability and willingness to accept connections.
Indicates current pipeline mode status of a connection.
Auth data hook event types for libpq authentication extensibility.
Opaque connection type to a PostgreSQL server. Contents are private to libpq.
Opaque type representing an asynchronous cancel connection associated with a PGconn.
Opaque query result handle returned by libpq functions. Freed with PQclear.
Opaque type used by legacy cancel APIs to cancel a running query on a PGconn.
Structure representing a NOTIFY message received on a connection. Public fields: relname, be_pid, extra. Instances are obtained from PQnotifies and must be freed with PQfreemem.
Time type representing microseconds since an unspecified epoch, used with PQsocketPoll and PQgetCurrentTimeUSec.
Callback type invoked by libpq for server notices; receives user arg and a PGresult containing notice details.
Callback type invoked for server notices as plain text messages.
Boolean-like type used in legacy printing options; char-sized flag values.
Options struct controlling formatting for PQprint and related legacy printing functions.
Descriptor of a single connection option as returned by PQconndefaults/PQconninfo/PQconninfoParse. Use PQconninfoFree to release arrays returned by those APIs.
Argument descriptor used with the legacy fast-path function PQfn.
Metadata about a single result column for constructing/modifying PGresult attributes with PQsetResultAttrs.
Callback type used to override libpq's internal thread lock for non-thread-safe libraries, typically Kerberos. Register with PQregisterThreadLock.
Struct describing data for OAuth device authorization prompts: verification URLs, user code, and expiration.
Hook-communication struct for custom OAuth Bearer token acquisition. Contains inputs (OIDC discovery URI, scope), optional async and cleanup callbacks, output token, and user state pointer.
Function type for authentication data hooks. Install with PQsetAuthDataHook.
Hook type used to supply an OpenSSL private key passphrase when libpq loads client keys.

functions.name: PQregisterEventProc
functions.signature: extern int PQregisterEventProc(PGconn *conn, PGEventProc proc, const char *name, void *passThrough);
functions.description: Register a libpq event callback (proc) on a connection. The callback will receive event notifications (register, conn reset/destroy, result create/copy/destroy). The name is for identification; passThrough is provided to the callback.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer (connected or being established).
proc must be a valid function pointer of type PGEventProc.
name should be a valid, null-terminated string (used for identification; content not otherwise specified).
May be called after creating PGconn and before it is destroyed.

functions.name: PQsetInstanceData
functions.signature: extern int PQsetInstanceData(PGconn *conn, PGEventProc proc, void *data);
functions.description: Associate application-defined instance data with a specific event proc on a given connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
proc must be an event proc previously known to the connection (typically registered via PQregisterEventProc).
data may be NULL or any pointer the application wants to associate.

functions.name: PQinstanceData
functions.description: Retrieve application-defined instance data associated with an event proc on a connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
proc identifies the event proc whose instance data is requested.

functions.name: PQresultSetInstanceData
functions.signature: extern int PQresultSetInstanceData(PGresult *result, PGEventProc proc, void *data);
functions.description: Associate application-defined instance data with a specific event proc on a PGresult.
requirements: result must be a valid PGresult pointer.
proc must be an event proc (registered on the associated connection).
data may be NULL or any application pointer.

functions.name: PQresultInstanceData
functions.description: Retrieve application-defined instance data associated with an event proc on a PGresult.
requirements: result must be a valid PGresult pointer.
proc identifies the event proc whose instance data is requested.

functions.name: PQfireResultCreateEvents
functions.description: Manually fire RESULTCREATE events for an application-created PGresult so event handlers can initialize per-result data.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
res must be a valid PGresult pointer created by the application.
Should be called after creating the PGresult and before it is used with event-related instance data.

functions.name: PQconnectStart
functions.description: Begin an asynchronous (non-blocking) connection to a server using a libpq conninfo string. Use PQconnectPoll to complete.
requirements: conninfo must be a null-terminated connection string or NULL for defaults.
Caller must drive the state machine with PQconnectPoll until completion or failure.

functions.name: PQconnectStartParams
functions.signature: extern PGconn *PQconnectStartParams(const char *const *keywords, const char *const *values, int expand_dbname);
functions.description: Begin an asynchronous connection using parallel keyword/value arrays. Use PQconnectPoll to complete. If expand_dbname is nonzero, dbname may be a connstring to expand.
requirements: keywords and values are parallel NULL-terminated arrays; each keywords[i] has values[i].
expand_dbname is typically 0 or 1.
Caller must poll with PQconnectPoll to finish connection.

functions.name: PQconnectPoll
functions.description: Advance a non-blocking connection started with PQconnectStart/Params. Returns a polling status indicating readiness or need to wait for read/write.
requirements: conn must be a PGconn returned by PQconnectStart/Params and not yet finished.
Caller must react to PGRES_POLLING_READING/WRITING using socket readiness before calling again.

functions.name: PQconnectdb
functions.description: Establish a blocking (synchronous) connection using a conninfo string. Returns a PGconn that may be in failure state; check PQstatus.
requirements: conninfo must be a null-terminated connection string or NULL for defaults.
Caller must check PQstatus(conn) for CONNECTION_OK before use and call PQfinish to free.

functions.name: PQconnectdbParams
functions.signature: extern PGconn *PQconnectdbParams(const char *const *keywords, const char *const *values, int expand_dbname);
functions.description: Establish a blocking connection using keyword/value arrays. Optionally expand dbname if expand_dbname is nonzero.
requirements: keywords and values are parallel NULL-terminated arrays.
Caller must check PQstatus for success and call PQfinish to free.

functions.name: PQsetdbLogin
functions.signature: extern PGconn *PQsetdbLogin(const char *pghost, const char *pgport, const char *pgoptions, const char *pgtty, const char *dbName, const char *login, const char *pwd);
functions.description: Legacy blocking connection routine accepting discrete parameters for host, port, options, tty, dbname, user, and password.
requirements: All strings must be valid null-terminated or NULL to accept defaults.
Deprecated macro PQsetdb wraps this with user and password as NULL.
Caller must check PQstatus and later PQfinish.

functions.name: PQfinish
functions.description: Close the connection and free the PGconn structure and associated resources.
requirements: conn may be NULL (no effect) or a valid PGconn pointer.
After calling, conn must not be used again.

functions.name: PQconndefaults
functions.description: Return an array of PQconninfoOption describing available connection options and their defaults. Free with PQconninfoFree.
requirements: Returned array must be freed with PQconninfoFree by the caller when no longer needed.
Pointers inside struct are as documented: static except val which is malloc'd.

functions.name: PQconninfoParse
functions.description: Parse a conninfo string into an array of PQconninfoOption like PQconndefaults. On parse errors, returns NULL and may set *errmsg.
requirements: conninfo may be NULL (use defaults) or a valid string.
If errmsg is non-NULL, on error it may be set to a malloc'd error string which the caller should free via PQfreemem.
Returned array must be freed with PQconninfoFree.

functions.name: PQconninfo
functions.description: Return the connection options actually in use by a live connection as an array of PQconninfoOption. Free with PQconninfoFree.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
Caller must free the returned array with PQconninfoFree.

functions.name: PQconninfoFree
functions.description: Free a PQconninfoOption array returned by PQconndefaults or PQconninfoParse, including any val strings.
requirements: connOptions may be NULL or a pointer previously returned by PQconndefaults, PQconninfoParse, or PQconninfo.
Must not be used on memory not obtained from those functions.

functions.name: PQresetStart
functions.description: Begin an asynchronous reset of an existing connection, closing and reestablishing with the same parameters. Use PQresetPoll to complete.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
Caller must poll with PQresetPoll until completion.

functions.name: PQresetPoll
functions.description: Advance a non-blocking connection reset started with PQresetStart. Indicates whether to wait for read/write or completion.
requirements: conn must be a PGconn on which PQresetStart was called.
Caller must handle PGRES_POLLING_READING/WRITING readiness before calling again.

functions.name: PQreset
functions.description: Synchronously reset a connection, closing and reestablishing with the same parameters.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
After return, check PQstatus to confirm success.

functions.name: PQcancelCreate
functions.description: Create a PGcancelConn used to cancel a query on the given PGconn asynchronously.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
Caller must eventually finish with PQcancelFinish to free resources.

functions.name: PQcancelStart
functions.description: Initiate a non-blocking cancel request on an existing PGcancelConn.
requirements: cancelConn must be a valid PGcancelConn created by PQcancelCreate.
Caller must use PQcancelPoll to drive progress to completion.

functions.name: PQcancelBlocking
functions.description: Issue a blocking cancel request using the provided PGcancelConn.
requirements: cancelConn must be a valid PGcancelConn.
Return value semantics are those of libpq (nonzero indicates success in libpq conventions; exact details not in header).

functions.name: PQcancelPoll
functions.description: Poll a non-blocking cancel request, returning the next action (read, write, ok, or failed).
requirements: cancelConn must be a valid PGcancelConn with a cancel in progress.

functions.name: PQcancelStatus
functions.description: Get status of the cancel connection object. Returns a ConnStatusType indicating its state.
requirements: cancelConn must be a valid PGcancelConn pointer.

functions.name: PQcancelSocket
functions.description: Obtain the underlying socket descriptor for a cancel connection, for use with polling APIs.
requirements: cancelConn must be a valid PGcancelConn pointer.

functions.name: PQcancelErrorMessage
functions.description: Return the last error message associated with the cancel connection.
requirements: cancelConn must be a valid PGcancelConn pointer.
Returned pointer is owned by libpq; do not free (ownership rules are implied by libpq conventions; header does not explicitly state).

functions.name: PQcancelReset
functions.description: Reset the cancel connection object, clearing any in-progress state.
requirements: cancelConn must be a valid PGcancelConn pointer.

functions.name: PQcancelFinish
functions.description: Finish and free a PGcancelConn created by PQcancelCreate.
requirements: cancelConn may be NULL or a valid PGcancelConn.
After return, cancelConn must not be used.

functions.name: PQgetCancel
functions.description: Create a legacy PGcancel object for cancelling a running query on a connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
Caller must free the object with PQfreeCancel.

functions.name: PQfreeCancel
functions.description: Free a PGcancel structure previously allocated by PQgetCancel.
requirements: cancel may be NULL or a valid PGcancel pointer obtained from PQgetCancel.
After return, pointer must not be used.

functions.name: PQcancel
functions.signature: extern int PQcancel(PGcancel *cancel, char *errbuf, int errbufsize);
functions.description: Deprecated, signal-safe cancellation using PGcancel. Writes any error message to errbuf.
requirements: cancel must be a valid PGcancel pointer.
errbuf must be a valid buffer of size errbufsize if provided; may be NULL with errbufsize 0 if caller ignores messages.
This is deprecated in favor of PQcancelBlocking.

functions.name: PQrequestCancel
functions.description: Deprecated, not thread-safe: request query cancellation on a connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
Deprecated; avoid in multithreaded contexts.

functions.name: PQdb
functions.description: Get the database name of the connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQuser
functions.description: Get the user name of the connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQpass
functions.description: Get the password associated with the connection, if available.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
Returned password is sensitive; handle carefully.

functions.name: PQhost
functions.description: Get the host name of the server for the connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQhostaddr
functions.description: Get the host address string for the connection, if available.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQport
functions.description: Get the server port as a string for the connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQtty
functions.description: Get the debugging tty option string for the connection (historical).
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQoptions
functions.description: Get the connection options string.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQstatus
functions.description: Return overall status of the connection (CONNECTION_OK, CONNECTION_BAD, etc.).
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQtransactionStatus
functions.description: Return current transaction status of the session (idle, active, in-transaction, etc.).
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQparameterStatus
functions.signature: extern const char *PQparameterStatus(const PGconn *conn, const char *paramName);
functions.description: Get the current value of a server parameter reported by the backend (e.g., server_version).
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
paramName must be a valid null-terminated parameter name string.

functions.name: PQprotocolVersion
functions.description: Return the frontend/backend protocol version in use.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQfullProtocolVersion
functions.description: Return the full protocol version, when available (v18+ feature).
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQserverVersion
functions.description: Return an integer representing the server's version number.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQerrorMessage
functions.description: Return the last error message for the connection as a string.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
Returned string is owned by libpq; do not free.

functions.name: PQsocket
functions.description: Return the underlying socket file descriptor for the connection, or -1 if unavailable.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQbackendPID
functions.description: Return the server process PID for this connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQpipelineStatus
functions.description: Return the current pipeline mode status (off, on, or aborted).
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQconnectionNeedsPassword
functions.description: Indicate whether the connection requires a password (e.g., authentication failed due to missing password).
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQconnectionUsedPassword
functions.description: Indicate whether a password was used for the current connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQconnectionUsedGSSAPI
functions.description: Indicate whether GSSAPI was used for the current connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQclientEncoding
functions.description: Get the current client encoding id for the connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQsetClientEncoding
functions.description: Set the client encoding for the connection by name.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
encoding must be a valid encoding name string supported by server/libpq.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: PQsslInUse
functions.description: Return nonzero if SSL/TLS is in use on the connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQsslStruct
functions.description: Return a pointer to an underlying SSL/TLS library-specific structure by name (e.g., "SSL").
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
struct_name must be a valid library-dependent identifier.

functions.name: PQsslAttribute
functions.description: Return a textual SSL/TLS attribute value for the connection by attribute name.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
attribute_name must be a supported attribute string.

functions.name: PQsslAttributeNames
functions.description: Return a NULL-terminated list of SSL/TLS attribute names supported by PQsslAttribute for the connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQgetssl
functions.description: Return the OpenSSL SSL* pointer for the connection, or NULL for unencrypted connections or non-OpenSSL TLS implementations.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
Only useful when OpenSSL is the TLS library.

functions.name: PQinitSSL
functions.description: Tell libpq whether it needs to initialize OpenSSL on its own. Back-compat helper.
requirements: do_init is nonzero to request libpq to initialize OpenSSL, zero to skip.

functions.name: PQinitOpenSSL
functions.signature: extern void PQinitOpenSSL(int do_ssl, int do_crypto);
functions.description: More detailed control over libpq's initialization of OpenSSL libraries for SSL and crypto.
requirements: do_ssl nonzero to initialize SSL support.
do_crypto nonzero to initialize OpenSSL crypto library.

functions.name: PQgssEncInUse
functions.description: Return nonzero if GSSAPI encryption is in use on the connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQgetgssctx
functions.description: Return the GSSAPI context for the connection if GSSAPI is in use, else NULL.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQsetErrorVerbosity
functions.description: Set error verbosity for PQerrorMessage and PQresultErrorMessage, returning the previous setting.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
verbosity must be a valid PGVerbosity enum value.

functions.name: PQsetErrorContextVisibility
functions.description: Control whether CONTEXT fields are included in error messages, returning previous setting.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
show_context must be a valid PGContextVisibility value.

functions.name: PQsetNoticeReceiver
functions.signature: extern PQnoticeReceiver PQsetNoticeReceiver(PGconn *conn, PQnoticeReceiver proc, void *arg);
functions.description: Override the default notice receiver callback for server notices/warnings. Returns previous receiver.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
proc may be NULL to restore defaults or a valid function pointer.
arg is passed to the callback.

functions.name: PQsetNoticeProcessor
functions.signature: extern PQnoticeProcessor PQsetNoticeProcessor(PGconn *conn, PQnoticeProcessor proc, void *arg);
functions.description: Override the default notice processor (string-based) callback. Returns previous processor.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
proc may be NULL to restore defaults or a valid function pointer.
arg is passed to the callback.

functions.name: PQregisterThreadLock
functions.description: Register a thread lock callback used internally by libpq to serialize non-threadsafe operations. Returns previous handler.
requirements: newhandler is a function taking int acquire; may be NULL to restore default internal mutex.
Only relevant for multithreaded apps using kerberos and libpq.

functions.name: PQtrace
functions.description: Enable libpq protocol trace output to the given FILE stream.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
debug_port must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.

functions.name: PQuntrace
functions.description: Disable libpq protocol tracing on the connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

functions.name: PQsetTraceFlags
functions.description: Set flags controlling PQtrace output formatting (e.g., suppress timestamps, regress mode).
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
flags is a bitmask using PQTRACE_* constants.

functions.name: PQexec
functions.description: Execute a SQL command synchronously; returns a PGresult for the command or query.
requirements: conn must be a valid, connected PGconn pointer.
query must be a valid null-terminated SQL string.
Caller must eventually PQclear the returned PGresult.

functions.name: PQexecParams
functions.signature: extern PGresult *PQexecParams(PGconn *conn, const char *command, int nParams, const Oid *paramTypes, const char *const *paramValues, const int *paramLengths, const int *paramFormats, int resultFormat);
functions.description: Execute a parameterized SQL command synchronously with specified parameter types/values and desired result format.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
command must be a valid SQL string.
nParams must be >= 0 and consistent with provided arrays.
paramTypes may be NULL or an array of length nParams.
paramValues/paramLengths/paramFormats must be NULL or arrays of length nParams as per libpq conventions.
resultFormat must be 0 (text) or 1 (binary).
Caller must PQclear the result.

functions.name: PQprepare
functions.signature: extern PGresult *PQprepare(PGconn *conn, const char *stmtName, const char *query, int nParams, const Oid *paramTypes);
functions.description: Create a named prepared statement on the server.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
stmtName must be a valid statement name string; empty for unnamed allowed by server rules.
query must be a valid SQL string.
nParams must be >= 0; paramTypes may be NULL or array of length nParams.
Caller must PQclear the result.

functions.name: PQexecPrepared
functions.signature: extern PGresult *PQexecPrepared(PGconn *conn, const char *stmtName, int nParams, const char *const *paramValues, const int *paramLengths, const int *paramFormats, int resultFormat);
functions.description: Execute a previously prepared statement synchronously with parameters.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.
stmtName must name an existing prepared statement.
nParams must match the statement's parameter count.
paramValues/paramLengths/paramFormats arrays must have nParams elements or be NULL as allowed by libpq.
resultFormat must be 0 or 1.
Caller must PQclear the result.

functions.name: PQsendQuery
functions.description: Start asynchronous execution of a SQL query. Retrieve results with PQgetResult.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer and not busy (PQisBusy==0).
query must be a valid SQL string.
Caller must consume results by repeatedly calling PQgetResult until NULL.

functions.name: PQsendQueryParams
functions.signature: extern int PQsendQueryParams(PGconn *conn, const char *command, int nParams, const Oid *paramTypes, const char *const *paramValues, const int *paramLengths, const int *paramFormats, int resultFormat);
functions.description: Asynchronously send a parameterized query. Results are retrieved with PQgetResult.
requirements: conn must be valid and not currently busy.
nParams must be >= 0 and arrays consistent.
resultFormat must be 0 or 1.
Caller must drain results using PQgetResult until NULL.

functions.name: PQsendPrepare
functions.signature: extern int PQsendPrepare(PGconn *conn, const char *stmtName, const char *query, int nParams, const Oid *paramTypes);
functions.description: Asynchronously create a prepared statement on the server.
requirements: conn must be valid and not busy.
stmtName and query must be valid strings.
nParams >= 0; paramTypes may be NULL or array of length nParams.
Caller must use PQgetResult to obtain command completion.

functions.name: PQsendQueryPrepared
functions.signature: extern int PQsendQueryPrepared(PGconn *conn, const char *stmtName, int nParams, const char *const *paramValues, const int *paramLengths, const int *paramFormats, int resultFormat);
functions.description: Asynchronously execute a prepared statement with parameters.
requirements: conn must be valid and not busy.
stmtName must identify a prepared statement.
nParams must match statement parameters; arrays as per libpq rules.
resultFormat 0 or 1.
Caller must read all results with PQgetResult.

functions.name: PQsetSingleRowMode
functions.description: Request single-row mode for the next query, causing PQgetResult to return one-row results incrementally.
requirements: conn must be valid and before reading results of the next query.
Only affects next query; must be called before sending/consuming that query's results.

functions.name: PQsetChunkedRowsMode
functions.description: Enable chunked-rows mode for the next query, returning results in chunks of up to chunkSize rows.
requirements: conn must be valid and before reading results of the next query.
chunkSize must be a positive integer.
Requires libpq with chunk mode support.

functions.name: PQgetResult
functions.description: Read the next PGresult from an asynchronous command queue; returns NULL when no more results remain.
requirements: conn must be valid.
Caller must PQclear each non-NULL PGresult returned.
Must be called until it returns NULL to finish a command cycle.

functions.name: PQisBusy
functions.description: Check whether a previous asynchronous operation is still being processed (i.e., results not yet ready).
requirements: conn must be valid.

functions.name: PQconsumeInput
functions.description: Read incoming data from the server and process it, without blocking if using nonblocking sockets.
requirements: conn must be valid.
Caller typically loops with PQisBusy and PQconsumeInput to progress.

functions.name: PQenterPipelineMode
functions.description: Enter pipeline mode, allowing batching of multiple commands without waiting for individual results.
requirements: conn must be valid and not already in pipeline mode.
Caller must eventually exit with PQexitPipelineMode.

functions.name: PQexitPipelineMode
functions.description: Exit pipeline mode on the connection.
requirements: conn must be valid and in pipeline mode.
All pending results should be drained before exiting to avoid errors.

functions.name: PQpipelineSync
functions.description: Insert a pipeline synchronization point, yielding a PGRES_PIPELINE_SYNC result when reached.
requirements: conn must be valid and in pipeline mode.

functions.name: PQsendFlushRequest
functions.description: Request that the client output buffer be flushed to the server (nonblocking).
requirements: conn must be valid.

functions.name: PQsendPipelineSync
functions.description: Send a pipeline synchronization message without leaving pipeline mode (v17+).
requirements: conn must be valid and in pipeline mode.

functions.name: PQnotifies
functions.description: Retrieve the next pending LISTEN/NOTIFY message as a PGnotify. Free with PQfreemem or PQfreeNotify.
requirements: conn must be valid.
Caller must free the returned PGnotify using PQfreemem (or PQfreeNotify macro).

functions.name: PQputCopyData
functions.signature: extern int PQputCopyData(PGconn *conn, const char *buffer, int nbytes);
functions.description: Send data during COPY IN operation from client to server.
requirements: conn must be valid and a COPY IN is in progress.
buffer must point to at least nbytes of data; nbytes >= 0.

functions.name: PQputCopyEnd
functions.description: Finish COPY IN. Optionally provide an error message to abort the COPY.
requirements: conn must be valid and currently in COPY IN state.
errormsg may be NULL to indicate success or a string to abort with error.

functions.name: PQgetCopyData
functions.signature: extern int PQgetCopyData(PGconn *conn, char **buffer, int async);
functions.description: Receive a data row during COPY OUT (or COPY BOTH) from server to client. Allocates buffer for caller to free with PQfreemem.
requirements: conn must be valid and in COPY OUT/BOTH state.
buffer must be a valid pointer to char*; libpq will allocate and assign when returning a row.
async controls blocking behavior (nonzero to avoid blocking).

functions.name: PQgetline
functions.signature: extern int PQgetline(PGconn *conn, char *buffer, int length);
functions.description: Deprecated: read a line of COPY data into buffer.
requirements: conn must be valid and COPY OUT state.
buffer must have at least length bytes.

functions.name: PQputline
functions.description: Deprecated: write a null-terminated string as COPY data.
requirements: conn must be valid and COPY IN state.
string must be a valid null-terminated string.

functions.name: PQgetlineAsync
functions.signature: extern int PQgetlineAsync(PGconn *conn, char *buffer, int bufsize);
functions.description: Deprecated: nonblocking attempt to read a line of COPY data.
requirements: conn must be valid.
buffer must have at least bufsize bytes.

functions.name: PQputnbytes
functions.signature: extern int PQputnbytes(PGconn *conn, const char *buffer, int nbytes);
functions.description: Deprecated: write exactly nbytes of COPY data from buffer.
requirements: conn must be valid and COPY IN state.
buffer must point to at least nbytes bytes; nbytes >= 0.

functions.name: PQendcopy
functions.description: Deprecated: finish copy in/out operation, older interface.
requirements: conn must be valid and a COPY is in progress.

functions.name: PQsetnonblocking
functions.description: Enable or disable nonblocking mode on the connection.
requirements: conn must be valid.
arg nonzero enables nonblocking, zero disables.

functions.name: PQisnonblocking
functions.description: Return whether the connection is in nonblocking mode.
requirements: conn must be valid.

functions.name: PQisthreadsafe
functions.description: Return whether the libpq library was built to be threadsafe.

functions.name: PQping
functions.description: Check if a server is accepting connections without establishing a session.
requirements: conninfo may be NULL or a valid connection string.

functions.name: PQpingParams
functions.signature: extern PGPing PQpingParams(const char *const *keywords, const char *const *values, int expand_dbname);
functions.description: Ping a server using keyword/value parameters to determine acceptability of connections.
requirements: keywords and values must be parallel NULL-terminated arrays.
expand_dbname controls dbname expansion.

functions.name: PQflush
functions.description: Try to flush the send buffer to the server.
requirements: conn must be valid.

functions.name: PQfn
functions.signature: extern PGresult *PQfn(PGconn *conn, int fnid, int *result_buf, int *result_len, int result_is_int, const PQArgBlock *args, int nargs);
functions.description: Call a backend function via the older fast-path interface. Not recommended for general use.
requirements: conn must be valid.
fnid must be a valid function OID number (as int).
args must be an array of PQArgBlock of length nargs; may be NULL if nargs==0.
If result_buf/result_len provided, they must point to valid storage.

functions.name: PQresultStatus
functions.description: Return the execution status code for a PGresult.
requirements: res must be a valid PGresult pointer.

functions.name: PQresStatus
functions.description: Return a string describing an ExecStatusType status code.
requirements: status must be a valid ExecStatusType value.

functions.name: PQresultErrorMessage
functions.description: Return the error message associated with a PGresult, if any.
requirements: res must be a valid PGresult pointer.
Returned string is owned by libpq; do not free.

functions.name: PQresultVerboseErrorMessage
functions.signature: extern char *PQresultVerboseErrorMessage(const PGresult *res, PGVerbosity verbosity, PGContextVisibility show_context);
functions.description: Return a verbose error message string for a result with specified verbosity and context visibility.
requirements: res must be a valid PGresult pointer.
verbosity and show_context must be valid enum values.
Returned string is owned by libpq; do not free.

functions.name: PQresultErrorField
functions.description: Return a specific field of the error report for a result, by field code (PG_DIAG_*).
requirements: res must be a valid PGresult pointer.
fieldcode must be one of the PG_DIAG_* constants.

functions.name: PQntuples
functions.description: Return the number of rows (tuples) in a result.
requirements: res must be a valid PGresult pointer.

functions.name: PQnfields
functions.description: Return the number of columns (fields) in a result.
requirements: res must be a valid PGresult pointer.

functions.name: PQbinaryTuples
functions.description: Indicate whether all result columns are in binary format.
requirements: res must be a valid PGresult pointer.

functions.name: PQfname
functions.description: Return the column name for a given field index.
requirements: res must be a valid PGresult pointer.
field_num must be in range [0, PQnfields(res)-1].

functions.name: PQfnumber
functions.signature: extern int PQfnumber(const PGresult *res, const char *field_name);
functions.description: Return the field index for a given column name, or -1 if not found.
requirements: res must be valid.
field_name must be a valid null-terminated string.

functions.name: PQftable
functions.signature: extern Oid PQftable(const PGresult *res, int field_num);
functions.description: Return the OID of the table from which a field was fetched, if known, else InvalidOid.
requirements: res must be valid.
field_num must be a valid field index.

functions.name: PQftablecol
functions.signature: extern int PQftablecol(const PGresult *res, int field_num);
functions.description: Return the column number within the table for a field, if known, else 0.
requirements: res must be valid.
field_num must be valid.

functions.name: PQfformat
functions.signature: extern int PQfformat(const PGresult *res, int field_num);
functions.description: Return the format code (0=text, 1=binary) for a field.
requirements: res must be valid.
field_num must be valid.

functions.name: PQftype
functions.signature: extern Oid PQftype(const PGresult *res, int field_num);
functions.description: Return the type OID of a field.
requirements: res must be valid.
field_num must be valid.

functions.name: PQfsize
functions.signature: extern int PQfsize(const PGresult *res, int field_num);
functions.description: Return the type size of a field (-1 for variable-length).
requirements: res must be valid.
field_num must be valid.

functions.name: PQfmod
functions.signature: extern int PQfmod(const PGresult *res, int field_num);
functions.description: Return the type modifier of a field, or -1 if not available.
requirements: res must be valid.
field_num must be valid.

functions.name: PQcmdStatus
functions.description: Return a command status tag string for a command result (e.g., INSERT 0 1).
requirements: res must be a valid PGresult pointer.
Returned string is owned by libpq; do not free.

functions.name: PQoidStatus
functions.description: Deprecated: return a string with the OID of the inserted row; use PQoidValue instead.
requirements: res must be valid.

functions.name: PQoidValue
functions.description: Return the OID of the row inserted by the most recent INSERT command in the result, or InvalidOid if not applicable.
requirements: res must be valid.

functions.name: PQcmdTuples
functions.description: Return the number of affected rows for a command as a string, or empty string if not applicable.
requirements: res must be valid.

functions.name: PQgetvalue
functions.signature: extern char *PQgetvalue(const PGresult *res, int tup_num, int field_num);
functions.description: Return a pointer to the field value at the given row and column, as a null-terminated string for text results or raw bytes for binary.
requirements: res must be valid.
tup_num must be in range [0, PQntuples(res)-1].
field_num must be in range [0, PQnfields(res)-1].
Pointer is valid until PQclear(res).

functions.name: PQgetlength
functions.signature: extern int PQgetlength(const PGresult *res, int tup_num, int field_num);
functions.description: Return the length in bytes of a field value.
requirements: res must be valid; tup_num and field_num must be in range.

functions.name: PQgetisnull
functions.signature: extern int PQgetisnull(const PGresult *res, int tup_num, int field_num);
functions.description: Test whether a field value is NULL.
requirements: res must be valid; tup_num and field_num must be in range.

functions.name: PQnparams
functions.description: Return the number of parameters of a prepared statement result (from Describe operations).
requirements: res must be valid.

functions.name: PQparamtype
functions.signature: extern Oid PQparamtype(const PGresult *res, int param_num);
functions.description: Return the type OID of a statement parameter by index.
requirements: res must be valid.
param_num must be in range [0, PQnparams(res)-1].

functions.name: PQdescribePrepared
functions.description: Synchronously describe a prepared statement, returning parameter and result metadata.
requirements: conn must be valid.
stmt must be a valid statement name string.
Caller must PQclear the result.

functions.name: PQdescribePortal
functions.description: Synchronously describe a portal (cursor), returning result metadata.
requirements: conn must be valid.
portal must be a valid portal name string.
Caller must PQclear the result.

functions.name: PQsendDescribePrepared
functions.description: Asynchronously request a description of a prepared statement.
requirements: conn must be valid and not busy.
stmt must be a valid statement name string.
Caller must read results with PQgetResult.

functions.name: PQsendDescribePortal
functions.description: Asynchronously request a description of a portal.
requirements: conn must be valid and not busy.
portal must be a valid portal name string.
Caller must read results with PQgetResult.

functions.name: PQclosePrepared
functions.description: Close a prepared statement on the server synchronously.
requirements: conn must be valid.
stmt must be a valid statement name string.
Caller must PQclear the result.

functions.name: PQclosePortal
functions.description: Close a portal (cursor) on the server synchronously.
requirements: conn must be valid.
portal must be a valid portal name string.
Caller must PQclear the result.

functions.name: PQsendClosePrepared
functions.description: Asynchronously close a prepared statement on the server.
requirements: conn must be valid and not busy.
stmt must be a valid statement name string.
Caller must read results with PQgetResult.

functions.name: PQsendClosePortal
functions.description: Asynchronously close a portal (cursor) on the server.
requirements: conn must be valid and not busy.
portal must be a valid portal name string.
Caller must read results with PQgetResult.

functions.name: PQclear
functions.description: Free a PGresult and all associated memory.
requirements: res may be NULL or a valid PGresult pointer.
After calling, res must not be used.

functions.name: PQfreemem
functions.description: Free memory allocated by libpq for results such as PGnotify or buffers from PQgetCopyData.
requirements: ptr may be NULL or a pointer obtained from libpq that requires PQfreemem.
Do not pass memory not allocated by libpq.

functions.name: PQmakeEmptyPGresult
functions.description: Create an empty PGresult with a given status, associated to a connection.
requirements: conn must be a valid PGconn pointer (may be used for context).
status must be a valid ExecStatusType.
Caller must PQclear the result.

functions.name: PQcopyResult
functions.description: Create a copy of a PGresult, optionally copying attributes, tuples, event associations, and notice hooks as per flags.
requirements: src must be a valid PGresult pointer.
flags is a bitmask of PG_COPYRES_* constants.
Caller must PQclear the returned result.

functions.name: PQsetResultAttrs
functions.signature: extern int PQsetResultAttrs(PGresult *res, int numAttributes, PGresAttDesc *attDescs);
functions.description: Set the result's attribute metadata (column descriptors).
requirements: res must be a valid PGresult pointer created by the application (e.g., via PQmakeEmptyPGresult).
numAttributes >= 0; attDescs must point to an array of length numAttributes.

functions.name: PQresultAlloc
functions.description: Allocate memory tied to the lifetime of a PGresult.
requirements: res must be valid.
nBytes > 0 to allocate memory; may return NULL on failure.
Memory is freed by PQclear(res).

functions.name: PQresultMemorySize
functions.description: Return the total memory footprint of a PGresult.
requirements: res must be valid.

functions.name: PQsetvalue
functions.signature: extern int PQsetvalue(PGresult *res, int tup_num, int field_num, char *value, int len);
functions.description: Set a field value in an application-constructed PGresult to the provided buffer of length len.
requirements: res must be a valid, mutable PGresult (e.g., created by the application).
tup_num and field_num must be within allocated ranges for the result.
value must point to at least len bytes; may be NULL to set NULL as per libpq behavior.

functions.name: PQescapeStringConn
functions.signature: extern size_t PQescapeStringConn(PGconn *conn, char *to, const char *from, size_t length, int *error);
functions.description: Escape a string literal for inclusion in SQL commands, using the connection's encoding and standard_conforming_strings setting.
requirements: conn must be valid.
to must point to a buffer large enough for the escaped output; worst-case 2*length+1 bytes.
from must point to input string bytes of given length.
error may be NULL or a pointer to receive 0/1 indicating error.

functions.name: PQescapeLiteral
functions.signature: extern char *PQescapeLiteral(PGconn *conn, const char *str, size_t len);
functions.description: Return a newly allocated, properly quoted literal for the given string. Caller must free with PQfreemem.
requirements: conn must be valid.
str must point to input bytes (not necessarily null-terminated if len provided).
Caller must free returned pointer with PQfreemem.

functions.name: PQescapeIdentifier
functions.signature: extern char *PQescapeIdentifier(PGconn *conn, const char *str, size_t len);
functions.description: Return a newly allocated, properly quoted SQL identifier for the given string. Caller must free with PQfreemem.
requirements: conn must be valid.
str must point to input bytes; len is its length.
Caller must free with PQfreemem.

functions.name: PQescapeByteaConn
functions.signature: extern unsigned char *PQescapeByteaConn(PGconn *conn, const unsigned char *from, size_t from_length, size_t *to_length);
functions.description: Escape binary data for bytea input syntax, returning a newly allocated buffer and its length.
requirements: conn must be valid.
from must point to from_length bytes.
to_length must be a valid pointer to receive output length.
Caller must free returned buffer with PQfreemem.

functions.name: PQunescapeBytea
functions.signature: extern unsigned char *PQunescapeBytea(const unsigned char *strtext, size_t *retbuflen);
functions.description: Decode a textual bytea representation to binary, returning a newly allocated buffer and its length.
requirements: strtext must point to a null-terminated bytea text string.
retbuflen must be a valid pointer to receive output length.
Caller must free returned buffer with PQfreemem.

functions.name: PQescapeString
functions.signature: extern size_t PQescapeString(char *to, const char *from, size_t length);
functions.description: Deprecated form of string escaping not aware of connection settings. Escapes input into 'to'.
requirements: to must have capacity >= 2*length+1 in worst case.
from must point to length bytes.

functions.name: PQescapeBytea
functions.signature: extern unsigned char *PQescapeBytea(const unsigned char *from, size_t from_length, size_t *to_length);
functions.description: Deprecated form of bytea escaping without connection context. Returns newly allocated escaped buffer.
requirements: from must point to from_length bytes.
to_length must be a valid pointer.
Caller must free returned buffer with PQfreemem.

functions.name: PQprint
functions.signature: extern void PQprint(FILE *fout, const PGresult *res, const PQprintOpt *po);
functions.description: Pretty-print a PGresult to a FILE stream with various formatting options.
requirements: fout must be a valid writable FILE*.
res must be a valid PGresult pointer.
po may be NULL or a valid options struct; strings inside must be valid if provided.

functions.name: PQdisplayTuples
functions.signature: extern void PQdisplayTuples(const PGresult *res, FILE *fp, int fillAlign, const char *fieldSep, int printHeader, int quiet);
functions.description: Legacy routine to display result tuples to a FILE with simple formatting.
requirements: res must be valid.
fp must be a writable FILE*.
fieldSep must be a valid string if non-NULL.

functions.name: PQprintTuples
functions.signature: extern void PQprintTuples(const PGresult *res, FILE *fout, int PrintAttNames, int TerseOutput, int colWidth);
functions.description: Legacy routine to print result tuples to a FILE with limited options.
requirements: res must be valid.
fout must be a writable FILE*.
colWidth >= 0.

functions.name: lo_open
functions.signature: extern int lo_open(PGconn *conn, Oid lobjId, int mode);
functions.description: Open a large object by OID, returning a large-object descriptor (fd) for subsequent lo_* operations.
requirements: conn must be valid.
lobjId must be a valid large object OID.
mode must be a valid open mode bitmask (per large object API; details not in header).

functions.name: lo_close
functions.description: Close a large-object descriptor obtained from lo_open.
requirements: conn must be valid.
fd must be a descriptor returned by lo_open on this connection.

functions.name: lo_read
functions.signature: extern int lo_read(PGconn *conn, int fd, char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Read up to len bytes from a large object into buf.
requirements: conn must be valid.
fd must be a valid large object descriptor.
buf must point to at least len bytes of writable memory.

functions.name: lo_write
functions.signature: extern int lo_write(PGconn *conn, int fd, const char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Write len bytes from buf to a large object.
requirements: conn must be valid.
fd must be a valid large object descriptor.
buf must point to at least len bytes.

functions.name: lo_lseek
functions.signature: extern int lo_lseek(PGconn *conn, int fd, int offset, int whence);
functions.description: Seek to a position within a large object using 32-bit offset.
requirements: conn must be valid.
fd must be a valid large object descriptor.
whence must be a valid SEEK_* value.
Offset range limited to 32-bit signed.

functions.name: lo_lseek64
functions.signature: extern int64_t lo_lseek64(PGconn *conn, int fd, int64_t offset, int whence);
functions.description: Seek within a large object using a 64-bit offset.
requirements: conn must be valid.
fd must be valid.
whence must be a valid SEEK_* value.

functions.name: lo_creat
functions.description: Create a new large object with server-chosen OID using legacy API.
requirements: conn must be valid.
mode is a creation mode; specifics are server-defined (header does not specify).

functions.name: lo_create
functions.description: Create a new large object with a specific OID.
requirements: conn must be valid.
lobjId is desired OID; may fail if already exists.

functions.name: lo_tell
functions.description: Return the current 32-bit seek position in a large object.
requirements: conn must be valid.
fd must be valid.

functions.name: lo_tell64
functions.description: Return the current 64-bit seek position in a large object.
requirements: conn must be valid.
fd must be valid.

functions.name: lo_truncate
functions.signature: extern int lo_truncate(PGconn *conn, int fd, size_t len);
functions.description: Truncate a large object to len bytes (size_t).
requirements: conn must be valid.
fd must be valid.
len is the target size; platform-dependent range.

functions.name: lo_truncate64
functions.signature: extern int lo_truncate64(PGconn *conn, int fd, int64_t len);
functions.description: Truncate a large object to a 64-bit length.
requirements: conn must be valid.
fd must be valid.

functions.name: lo_unlink
functions.description: Delete a large object by OID.
requirements: conn must be valid.
lobjId must identify an existing large object.

functions.name: lo_import
functions.description: Import a file from the client filesystem as a new large object; returns its OID.
requirements: conn must be valid.
filename must be a valid path accessible to the client process.

functions.name: lo_import_with_oid
functions.signature: extern Oid lo_import_with_oid(PGconn *conn, const char *filename, Oid lobjId);
functions.description: Import a file as a large object with a specified OID.
requirements: conn must be valid.
filename must be a valid path.
lobjId is desired OID; may fail if taken.

functions.name: lo_export
functions.signature: extern int lo_export(PGconn *conn, Oid lobjId, const char *filename);
functions.description: Export a large object to a client-side file.
requirements: conn must be valid.
lobjId must exist.
filename must be a writable path accessible to the client process.

functions.name: PQlibVersion
functions.description: Return the version of the libpq library in use as an integer.

functions.name: PQsocketPoll
functions.signature: extern int PQsocketPoll(int sock, int forRead, int forWrite, pg_usec_time_t end_time);
functions.description: Poll a socket for readability and/or writability until the specified absolute end time (in microseconds), or immediately if end_time has passed.
requirements: sock must be a valid socket descriptor.
forRead and forWrite are booleans (0/1) indicating interest.
end_time is an absolute time as returned by PQgetCurrentTimeUSec.

functions.name: PQgetCurrentTimeUSec
functions.description: Return the current time in microseconds since an unspecified epoch, suitable for PQsocketPoll end_time.

functions.name: PQmblen
functions.signature: extern int PQmblen(const char *s, int encoding);
functions.description: Determine length in bytes of the multibyte character at s for the given encoding.
requirements: s must point to a valid character sequence in the given encoding.
encoding must be a valid encoding id.

functions.name: PQmblenBounded
functions.signature: extern int PQmblenBounded(const char *s, int encoding);
functions.description: Like PQmblen but not more than the remaining string length; safer for scanning.
requirements: s must point to a valid string.
encoding must be a valid encoding id.

functions.name: PQdsplen
functions.signature: extern int PQdsplen(const char *s, int encoding);
functions.description: Determine the display width (columns) of the multibyte character at s for the given encoding.
requirements: s must point to a valid character sequence.
encoding must be a valid encoding id.

functions.name: PQenv2encoding
functions.description: Return the encoding id inferred from the environment variable PGCLIENTENCODING.

functions.name: PQencryptPassword
functions.description: Return a newly allocated string containing a server-compatible hashed password for a user, using default algorithm.
requirements: passwd and user must be valid null-terminated strings.
Caller must free returned string with PQfreemem.

functions.name: PQencryptPasswordConn
functions.signature: extern char *PQencryptPasswordConn(PGconn *conn, const char *passwd, const char *user, const char *algorithm);
functions.description: Return a newly allocated string with a hashed password using connection context and specified algorithm.
requirements: conn must be valid (may be used for settings).
passwd and user must be valid strings.
algorithm must be a valid algorithm name supported by server/libpq.
Caller must free with PQfreemem.

functions.name: PQchangePassword
functions.signature: extern PGresult *PQchangePassword(PGconn *conn, const char *user, const char *passwd);
functions.description: Change the password of the specified user using the connection.
requirements: conn must be valid and connected with privileges to change the password.
user and passwd must be valid strings.
Caller must PQclear the returned result.

functions.name: PQsetAuthDataHook
functions.description: Install a libpq authentication data hook used to supply additional auth data (e.g., OAuth).
requirements: hook may be NULL to clear or a valid callback conforming to PQauthDataHook_type.

functions.name: PQgetAuthDataHook
functions.description: Retrieve the currently installed authentication data hook.

functions.name: PQdefaultAuthDataHook
functions.signature: extern int PQdefaultAuthDataHook(PGauthData type, PGconn *conn, void *data);
functions.description: Default implementation of the authentication data hook for built-in behaviors.
requirements: type must be a valid PGauthData enum.
conn must be valid.
data must be a pointer appropriate for the requested type (e.g., PGoauthBearerRequest for PQAUTHDATA_OAUTH_BEARER_TOKEN).

functions.name: pg_char_to_encoding
functions.description: Map an encoding name string to an encoding id.
requirements: name must be a valid encoding name string.

functions.name: pg_encoding_to_char
functions.description: Return the canonical name string for an encoding id.
requirements: encoding must be a valid encoding id.

functions.name: pg_valid_server_encoding_id
functions.description: Return nonzero if the encoding id is a valid server encoding.
requirements: encoding is an integer encoding id.

functions.name: PQgetSSLKeyPassHook_OpenSSL
functions.description: Get the currently set OpenSSL private key passphrase callback used by libpq.

functions.name: PQsetSSLKeyPassHook_OpenSSL
functions.description: Set the OpenSSL private key passphrase callback used by libpq.
requirements: hook may be NULL to restore default or a valid function pointer of type PQsslKeyPassHook_OpenSSL_type.

functions.name: PQdefaultSSLKeyPassHook_OpenSSL
functions.signature: extern int PQdefaultSSLKeyPassHook_OpenSSL(char *buf, int size, PGconn *conn);
functions.description: Default passphrase callback that libpq can use to obtain an SSL key passphrase into buf.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of length at least size.
size must be > 0.
conn must be a valid PGconn pointer.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces C-style identifier/name strings suitable for libpq APIs
# such as event proc names, prepared statement names, and portal names.
# Goals:
# - Always valid null-terminated strings when interpreted by C (we return bytes including a trailing NUL).
# - Cover interesting categories that may exercise different internal paths:
#   * Empty string
#   * Short ASCII identifiers
#   * Strings with spaces and punctuation
#   * Quoted identifiers and mixed case
#   * Very long names near typical internal limits
#   * Non-ASCII UTF-8 (multibyte) sequences
#   * Strings with SQL-like special characters
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_LETTERS_DIGITS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
IDENT_START = string.ascii_letters + "_"
IDENT_CONT = IDENT_START + string.digits
PUNCT = "-_./:+@#%[]{}()$^&!?,;|~"
SQL_SPECIAL = "\"'` \\\t\n"  # quote, apostrophe, backtick, space, backslash, tab, newline

UTF8_SAMPLES = [
    "αβγ",            # Greek
    "Русский",        # Cyrillic
    "日本語",          # Japanese
    "한국어",          # Korean
    "𝔘𝔫𝔦𝔠𝔬𝔡𝔢",       # Fraktur letters (surrogates in UTF-16, valid UTF-8)
    "😀😇🤖",          # Emoji
    "ñáéíóúüç",      # Latin accented
]

# Helper to build a SQL-like identifier (unquoted)
def make_unquoted_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 32) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    if n <= 0:
        return ""
    first = rng.choice(IDENT_START)
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(IDENT_CONT) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return first + rest

# Helper to build a mixed string including punctuation and spaces
def make_mixed(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    alphabet = ASCII_LETTERS_DIGITS + PUNCT + SQL_SPECIAL
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

# Helper to build a quoted identifier (with internal quotes doubled)
def make_quoted_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 0, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    inner_len = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    inner_alphabet = ASCII_LETTERS_DIGITS + PUNCT + " "
    inner = ''.join(rng.choice(inner_alphabet) for _ in range(inner_len))
    # Double quotes for SQL identifier-style quoting
    inner = inner.replace('"', '""')
    return f'"{inner}"'

# Helper to pick a UTF-8 sample and optionally augment
def make_utf8(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 128) -> str:
    base = rng.choice(UTF8_SAMPLES)
    # Optionally interleave ASCII and punctuation
    parts: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5)):
        parts.append(base)
        # small ASCII chunk
        parts.append(make_unquoted_ident(rng, 1, 6))
        # maybe punctuation
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(rng.choice(PUNCT))
    s = ''.join(parts)
    if len(s) > max_len:
        s = s[:max_len]
    return s

# Construct a scenario-specific identifier likely to pass/fail meaningfully
def make_scenario_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    scenarios = []
    # 0: empty string (valid C-string; some APIs may allow empty names)
    scenarios.append("")
    # 1: short ascii identifier
    scenarios.append(make_unquoted_ident(rng, 1, 12))
    # 2: mixed content with spaces and punctuation
    scenarios.append(make_mixed(rng, 3, 40))
    # 3: quoted identifier with doubled quotes
    scenarios.append(make_quoted_ident(rng, 0, 30))
    # 4: long name near limit (e.g., ~256)
    long_len = rng.randint(200, 300)
    long_body = ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_LETTERS_DIGITS + "_") for _ in range(long_len))
    scenarios.append(long_body)
    # 5: UTF-8 rich name
    scenarios.append(make_utf8(rng, 120))
    # 6: SQL-ish name that looks like a statement identifier
    scenarios.append("stmt_" + make_unquoted_ident(rng, 4, 32))
    # 7: portal-like name with punctuation
    scenarios.append("portal:" + make_mixed(rng, 2, 20))
    # 8: name with path-like segments
    scenarios.append("ns/schema/" + make_unquoted_ident(rng, 3, 24))
    # 9: name with backslashes and whitespace
    scenarios.append(make_mixed(rng, 5, 50).replace("\n", " ").replace("\t", " "))

    return rng.choice(scenarios)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    s = make_scenario_string(rng)

    # Ensure total size including NUL <= MAX_TOTAL. If longer, truncate safely on code point boundary.
    # Python slicing of str is by code point; encode to UTF-8 afterward.
    # Leave room for trailing NUL.
    max_chars = MAX_TOTAL - 1  # bytes budget for UTF-8 may exceed chars; enforce on bytes after encoding
    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) >= MAX_TOTAL:
        # Truncate by progressively reducing characters to fit in bytes budget
        # Conservative approach: shrink by factor until fits
        lo, hi = 0, len(s)
        # Binary search maximum prefix that fits
        while lo < hi:
            mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
            if len(s[:mid].encode('utf-8')) < MAX_TOTAL:
                lo = mid
            else:
                hi = mid - 1
        b = s[:lo].encode('utf-8')
    # Append C-string terminator
    return b + b"\x00"

    # sometimes inject quoted values or with spaces to test parsing
    base = rng.choice(GENERIC_VALUES)
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        return b'"' + base + b'"'
    return base

    for key, val in curated[:2]:

        while key in used_keys and tries < 3:
            key = _pick_keyword(rng)
            tries += 1
        used_keys.add(key)
        val = _pick_value(rng, key)
        parts.append(key)
        parts.append(val)

    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        key = b"user"
        parts.append(key)
        parts.append(rng.choice([b"postgres", b"", b"fuzz"]))
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        key = b"password"
        parts.append(key)

    if rng.random() < 0.5:

    if len(payload) > 4096:

        while parts and len(_cstr(parts)) > 4096:

OPTIONS_SAMPLES = [
    "",  # none
    "-c statement_timeout=5000",
    "-c search_path=public",
    "-c application_name=fuzzseed",
]

TTY_SAMPLES = [
    "",  # historical/unused; keep mostly empty
    "/dev/tty",
]

DBNAME_SAMPLES = [
    "",           # default user/db
    "postgres",
    "template1",
    "db1",
    "test-db",
    "db with space",
]

USER_SAMPLES = [
    "",          # default from env/system
    "postgres",
    "pguser",
    "user_with_ü",  # multibyte client encoding path
]

PASS_SAMPLES = [
    "",              # no password
    "secret",
    "pa$$w0rd",
    "longpasswordlongpasswordlongpassword",
]

def rand_hostname(r: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = r.randrange(0, 6)
    if choice == 0:
        return r.choice(HOST_SAMPLES)
    if choice == 1:
        # Random IPv4
        ip = ipaddress.IPv4Address(r.randrange(0, 2**32))
        return str(ip)
    if choice == 2:
        # Random IPv6, sometimes bracketed
        ip = ipaddress.IPv6Address(r.getrandbits(128))
        s = str(ip)
        return f"[{s}]" if r.random() < 0.5 else s
    if choice == 3:
        # Random hostname label set
        labels = []
        n = r.randint(1, 4)
        for _ in range(n):
            lablen = r.randint(1, 15)
            # start/end alnum, interior may include hyphen
            chars = []
            for i in range(lablen):
                if i == 0 or i == lablen - 1:
                    chars.append(r.choice("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"))
                else:
                    chars.append(r.choice("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-"))
            labels.append("".join(chars))
        return ".".join(labels)
    if choice == 4:
        # UNIX socket directory typical paths
        return r.choice(["/tmp", "/var/run/postgresql", "/run/postgresql"])
    # default curated
    return r.choice(HOST_SAMPLES)


def pick(r: random.Random, arr: List[str]) -> str:
    return arr[r.randrange(0, len(arr))]


def make_bits(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bit layout in stub:
    # 0x01 host, 0x02 port, 0x04 options, 0x08 tty, 0x10 db, 0x20 user, 0x40 pass
    # We want a spread of NULL vs provided. Ensure at least host or port is provided sometimes,
    # but also allow all NULL occasionally to test defaults.
    if r.random() < 0.15:
        return 0  # all NULL => full defaults path
    bits = 0
    for mask in (0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08, 0x10, 0x20, 0x40):
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            bits |= mask
    # Ensure some cases specifically test host-only, port-only, both, etc.
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        # host only
        bits = (bits | 0x01) & ~0x02
    elif r.random() < 0.4:
        # port only
        bits = (bits | 0x02) & ~0x01
    elif r.random() < 0.6:
        # both host and port
        bits |= 0x03
    return bits


def nz(s: str) -> bytes:
    return s.encode("utf-8", "surrogatepass") + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    bits = make_bits(r)

    # Hostname string: prioritize valid formats
    host = rand_hostname(r)

    # Port string: numeric or empty
    port = pick(r, PORT_SAMPLES)

    # Options/tty/db/user/pass: mix of curated and small randoms
    opts = pick(r, OPTIONS_SAMPLES)
    tty = pick(r, TTY_SAMPLES)
    db = pick(r, DBNAME_SAMPLES)
    user = pick(r, USER_SAMPLES)
    pwd = pick(r, PASS_SAMPLES)

    # Occasionally craft connection options to include multiple -c flags
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        extra = pick(r, ["-c plan_cache_mode=force_generic_plan", "-c search_path=pg_catalog,public"])  # simple extras
        opts = (opts + " " + extra).strip()

    # Ensure total size <= 4096 bytes
    parts = [
        struct.pack("<I", bits),
        nz(host),
        nz(port),
        nz(opts),
        nz(tty),
        nz(db),
        nz(user),
        nz(pwd),
    ]
    out = b"".join(parts)
    if len(out) > 4096:
        # Trim by shortening the longest textual fields conservatively
        def trim(s: bytes, maxlen: int) -> bytes:
            if len(s) <= maxlen:
                return s
            # keep NUL terminator
            return s[: maxlen - 1] + b"\x00"
        budget = 4096
        # keep bits intact
        b_parts = parts
        # Try progressively smaller caps
        caps = [256, 128, 64, 32]
        for cap in caps:
            b_parts = [b_parts[0]] + [trim(p, cap) for p in b_parts[1:]]
            out = b"".join(b_parts)
            if len(out) <= budget:
                break
    return out

# Target data type: "port string" for PQsetdbLogin's pgport parameter.
# We want to generate interesting, but valid, null-terminated strings that represent
# server port numbers. The fuzzer stub will call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() multiple times
# to populate host/port/options/tty/db/user/pass. Our generator supplies a single
# initial buffer which the harness will slice for each FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME.
# Therefore, we should pack multiple candidate strings in sequence, separated by NULs,
# so that each FUZZ_PARAM_STR() can consume a meaningful value. We will include many
# port-like strings (numeric, edge cases, IPv6-style service names not valid as ports
# but still strings), along with empty strings. The harness may map any of them to
# the 'port' position depending on the random bitfield in the stub.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

DIGITS = string.digits


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(len(items))]


def _gen_numeric_port(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Valid TCP/UDP ports are 0-65535. libpq typically expects a string of digits.
    # Generate typical values and boundary cases.
    choices = [
        "",              # empty
        "0",             # boundary
        "1",
        "9",
        "10",
        "79",
        "80",
        "110",
        "111",
        "123",
        "256",
        "512",
        "1023",
        "1024",
        "2048",
        "2376",
        "3000",
        "3306",
        "4000",
        "4444",
        "5000",
        "5431",
        "5432",         # PostgreSQL default
        "5433",
        "5672",
        "6000",
        "6379",
        "6432",         # pgbouncer
        "65000",
        "65534",
        "65535",        # upper boundary
    ]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return _rand_choice(rng, choices)
    # Or generate a random numeric within range (sometimes leading zeros)
    val = rng.randrange(0, 65536)
    s = str(val)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        # add leading zeros randomly
        width = rng.randrange(len(s), min(len(s) + 3, 6))
        s = s.zfill(width)
    return s


def _gen_service_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Some users pass service names; libpq supports "service" via conn params,
    # but pgport expects digits. Still, a string remains valid input.
    names = [
        "postgresql", "pgsql", "postgres", "db", "service", "prod", "dev", "test",
        "pg", "pg-main", "pg-alt", "pgbouncer", "tls", "ssl", "gssapi"
    ]
    # Occasionally include digits mixed in
    base = _rand_choice(rng, names)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base += str(rng.randrange(0, 10000))
    return base


def _gen_with_whitespace(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Ports as strings with accidental whitespace; still a valid C-string
    core = _gen_numeric_port(rng)
    pads = ["", " ", "\t", "\r", "\n"]
    return _rand_choice(rng, pads) + core + _rand_choice(rng, pads)


def _gen_plusminus(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Signed numeric forms (not typical, but numeric characters with a sign)
    sign = _rand_choice(rng, ["+", "-"])
    return sign + _gen_numeric_port(rng).lstrip()


def _gen_long_numeric(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Very long numeric string (still digits), to test length handling
    length = rng.randrange(6, 32)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(DIGITS) for _ in range(length))


def _gen_unicode_digits(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Include Unicode digits mixed with ASCII digits; still a valid UTF-8 C-string
    # Examples: Arabic-Indic digits U+0660..U+0669
    arabic_indic = [chr(c) for c in range(0x0660, 0x066A)]
    s = []
    for _ in range(rng.randrange(2, 8)):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            s.append(rng.choice(DIGITS))
        else:
            s.append(rng.choice(arabic_indic))
    return ''.join(s)


def _gen_candidate_list(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []
    # Core valid numeric ports and boundaries
    for _ in range(rng.randrange(4, 10)):
        out.append(_gen_numeric_port(rng))
    # Variants that are still strings and may exercise parsing paths
    out.extend([
        _gen_with_whitespace(rng),
        _gen_with_whitespace(rng),
        _gen_service_like(rng),
        _gen_service_like(rng),
        _gen_plusminus(rng),
        _gen_long_numeric(rng),
        _gen_unicode_digits(rng),
        "",  # empty string explicitly
    ])
    # Ensure we include the canonical default
    if "5432" not in out:
        out.insert(0, "5432")
    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    deduped = []
    for s in out:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            deduped.append(s)
    return deduped


def _pack_null_terminated(strings: List[str], limit: int) -> bytes:
    # Join strings with NUL separators and ensure final NUL termination for each consumer.
    b = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        enc = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        # Ensure each string is reasonably bounded to avoid exceeding total
        if len(enc) > 512:
            enc = enc[:512]
        if len(b) + len(enc) + 1 > limit:
            break
        b.extend(enc)
        b.append(0)
    # Guarantee at least one NUL if empty
    if not b:
        b.append(0)
    return bytes(b)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    candidates = _gen_candidate_list(rng)
    # Shuffle to vary assignment across FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls
    rng.shuffle(candidates)
    # Also prepend a few empty strings so that sometimes parameters become empty
    prefix_empties = [""] * rng.randrange(1, 4)
    payload = prefix_empties + candidates
    data = _pack_null_terminated(payload, min(MAX_TOTAL, 4096))
    return data

import string
from typing import List

# Generator for valid PostgreSQL username strings (roles). The fuzz stubs
# pass these to: PQsetdbLogin (login), PQencryptPassword(user),
# PQencryptPasswordConn(user), PQchangePassword(user).
#
# PostgreSQL role names are identifiers. They can be unquoted simple identifiers
# (letters, digits, underscores, $) starting with a non-digit, or any text when
# quoted with double quotes. Libpq APIs here expect plain C strings; the server
# will parse them as identifiers in SQL context, so producing both unquoted and
# quoted forms is interesting while remaining valid.
# Also include common usernames and lengths near boundaries (short, long) and
# a range of ASCII/UTF-8 characters in quoted identifiers.

MAX_LEN = 128  # keep small; well under libpq practical limits

_simple_start = string.ascii_letters + "_" + "$"
_simple_body = _simple_start + string.digits

# Reasonable set of Unicode characters that PostgreSQL accepts in quoted identifiers.
# Keep bytes manageable and valid UTF-8.
_unicode_supp = [
    "ä", "ö", "ü", "ß", "é", "è", "ñ", "ç", "ø", "å", "Ω", "π", "中", "文", "日本", "語",
]

_common_usernames = [
    "postgres", "pgadmin", "admin", "root", "user", "test", "tester", "readonly",
    "readwrite", "replication", "monitor", "backup", "owner", "app", "service",
]

# Some interesting quoted patterns, including embedded quotes escaped by doubling
# and whitespace or special characters that require quoting.
_special_chunks = [
    "with space", "mixedCase", "dash-name", "dot.name", "name@domain", "name:role",
    "semi;colon", "comma,sep", "paren(open)", "paren)close", "[brackets]", "{brace}",
    "quote\"inside", "two""quotes",  # this string literal contains doubled quotes already
]


def _rand_weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return rng.choice(items)


def _make_simple_identifier(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = MAX_LEN) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max(1, min(max_len, 24)))  # typical short names
    start = rng.choice(_simple_start)
    body = "".join(rng.choice(_simple_body) for _ in range(length - 1))
    return start + body


def _escape_sql_identifier_fragment(s: str) -> str:
    # In SQL, double quotes are escaped by doubling them inside quoted identifiers
    return s.replace('"', '""')


def _make_quoted_identifier(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a quoted identifier with a mix of ascii, unicode, and specials
    parts: List[str] = []
    # choose number of fragments
    nfrag = rng.randint(1, 3)
    for _ in range(nfrag):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.4:
            frag = _make_simple_identifier(rng, 1, 12)
        elif choice < 0.7:
            frag = _rand_weighted_choice(rng, _special_chunks)
        else:
            frag = rng.choice(_unicode_supp)
        parts.append(frag)
    inner = " ".join(parts)
    inner = _escape_sql_identifier_fragment(inner)
    return f'"{inner}"'


def _edge_case_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate edge cases: minimal length, max length, many $ or _
    pick = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if pick == 0:
        return rng.choice(string.ascii_letters)
    if pick == 1:
        # near maximum simple identifier length
        L = rng.randint(60, min(63, MAX_LEN))  # classic NAMEDATALEN default is 64 incl NUL; server may fold
        start = rng.choice(_simple_start)
        body = "".join(rng.choice(_simple_body) for _ in range(L - 1))
        return start + body
    if pick == 2:
        return "_" * rng.randint(1, 16)
    if pick == 3:
        return "$" + "x" * rng.randint(0, 8)  # like $x functions or dollar prefixes
    return _make_quoted_identifier(rng)


def _maybe_schema_qualified(rng: random.Random, ident: str) -> str:
    # Sometimes return schema-qualified user like "schema.user" though roles don't use schemas, but
    # for SQL contexts it's valid as an identifier shape; keep mostly simple to remain valid usernames.
    # Prefer just the role name; occasionally return a quoted form to test parser paths in hashing APIs.
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        left = _make_simple_identifier(rng, 1, 16)
        right = ident if rng.random() < 0.5 else _make_simple_identifier(rng, 1, 16)
        return f'"{left}"."{right}"'  # still a single string; server may reject in some contexts but is valid text
    return ident


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide generation strategy
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.25:
        name = _rand_weighted_choice(rng, _common_usernames)
    elif roll < 0.55:
        name = _make_simple_identifier(rng)
    elif roll < 0.85:
        name = _make_quoted_identifier(rng)
    else:
        name = _edge_case_name(rng)

    # Occasionally schema-qualify or keep as is; aim to stay valid as plain username text.
    name = _maybe_schema_qualified(rng, name)

    # Enforce a reasonable upper bound and ensure not empty
    if not name:
        name = "postgres"
    if len(name.encode('utf-8')) > 256:
        # if too long after Unicode expansion, trim inside quotes if any
        if name.startswith('"') and name.endswith('"') and len(name) > 2:
            inner = name[1:-1]
            inner_bytes = inner.encode('utf-8')[:200]
            try:
                inner = inner_bytes.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
            except Exception:
                inner = "trimmed"
            name = f'"{inner}"'
        else:
            name = name.encode('utf-8')[:200].decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
            if not name:
                name = "user"

    # Return as bytes with a terminating NUL not required by fuzz infra, but libpq expects C-string.
    # The fuzz harness passes std::string.c_str(), which is NUL-terminated by definition.
    data = name.encode('utf-8')
    return data[:4096]

# Helper to choose a mixture and build a NUL-separated blob ending with a final NUL

def _build_blob(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:

def _random_ascii_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    first_chars = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz_"
    rest_chars = first_chars + "0123456789-:/()._[] "
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)

    choice = rng.random()
